index.testimonial1: httpSMS is free platform which transforms your phone into an sms server! It has no hard limit also. It is an innovative idea, I have not seen such tech before. If you have an sms active pack in your phone then good to go with httpSMS.
index.testimonial2: "Outstanding product. Literally have been using this for years since we don't have an sms gateways that can handle http requests costing less than 50 cent per sms in my Country. Love the product and the support! Great work Arnold!"
index.faqDesc: If you still cannot find the answer to your question, open an issue on GitHub.
index.faq1Question: Can I install the app on my iPhone?
index.faq1Answer: The httpSMS application works only on Android phones at the moment since Apple doesn't allow you to install a custom SMS messaging app.
index.faq2Question: What's the minimum supported Android version?
index.faq2Answer: The httpSMS Android app works from Android 9 (Pie) and above. So you can install the application on your old Android phone which you don't use anymore.
index.faq3Question: Can I send unlimited number of messages per month?
index.faq3Answer: Yes. This project is 100% free and self-hosted: there are no paid plans and no message limits. The only limit is the one set by your carrier or SIM card.
index.faq4Question: Can I change the sender of the SMS message?
index.faq4Answer: No you cannot. When you send an SMS message using the httpSMS app it uses your SIM card to send the message so the recipient will see your phone number as the sender of the SMS. You cannot use your brand name as the sender ID.

privacy.metaDescription: What data httpSMS, free self-hosted software to send and receive SMS from an Android phone, processes, who is responsible for it and how to delete it.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

intro.p1: httpSMS is free and open-source software that turns an Android phone into an SMS gateway: you can send and receive text messages through an HTTP API and a web dashboard. Anyone can install it for free on their own server; there are no paid plans, payments or subscriptions.
intro.p2: This policy explains what data the software processes, what it is used for and who is responsible for it. It applies to the httpSMS installation where you are reading it. We call the person or organization that installs and runs that installation the “operator”, and the people who develop the open-source project the “maintainers”.

controller.title: Who is responsible for your data
controller.p1: There is no central httpSMS service. Each installation runs on its operator's server, and the data is stored there: in the operator's database and in the services the operator has configured.
controller.p2: That is why the operator of each installation is the data controller for the personal data processed in it. The project maintainers do not run third-party installations and have no access to their data.

data.title: Data the software processes
data.p1: To work, httpSMS stores and processes the following data on the operator's server:

account.label: Account:
account.text: email address, name and profile picture (if the sign-in provider shares them), Firebase Authentication user ID, time zone and notification preferences.

phones.label: Phones:
phones.text: phone number, SIM in use, push notification token (FCM) and each phone's settings, such as the messages-per-minute limit, send schedules or retries.

messages.label: Messages:
messages.text: content of sent and received SMS, sender and recipient numbers, timestamps, delivery status, failure reasons and, where applicable, attachments.

contacts.label: Contacts and threads:
contacts.text: your contacts' numbers and names, and conversations with their state (read, archived).

heartbeats.label: Heartbeats and device data:
heartbeats.text: periodic signals sent by the Android app with the time, the app version and whether the phone is charging, plus events such as missed calls when the app reports them.

apiKeys.label: API keys:
apiKeys.text: your account API key and any phone API keys you create.

integrations.label: Webhooks and integrations:
integrations.text: your webhook URLs, their signing keys and the data of any optional integrations you connect (for example, Discord).

logs.label: Technical logs:
logs.text: request data such as IP address, browser or client, date and result, which may be kept in the application logs for security and troubleshooting.

encryption.title: End-to-end encryption (optional)
encryption.p1: httpSMS lets you encrypt message content with a key that you set in the Android app and in your own application. When you use this feature, the content travels and is stored encrypted, and the server cannot read it.
encryption.p2: The server still sees the data it needs to deliver messages, such as phone numbers, timestamps and status. If you lose your key, nobody can recover the encrypted content.

uses.title: How the data is used
uses.p1: The software uses this data only to:

items.i1: Send and receive SMS through your phone and show them in the web dashboard.
items.i2: Notify your phone, through push notifications, that there are messages to send.
items.i3: Deliver events to your webhooks and integrations.
items.i4: Send you service emails, such as phone-offline or API-key-change alerts, if the operator has configured an email server.
items.i5: Protect the installation from abuse and troubleshoot errors.

uses.closing: httpSMS shows no ads and does not sell data. If the operator adds other tools, such as analytics, they should disclose it in their own version of this policy.

providers.title: Third-party services
providers.p1: A standard httpSMS installation relies on the following services. Some are optional and are only used if the operator configures them. Each provider has its own privacy policy:

items.firebaseAuth: sign-in to the web dashboard (email, Google or other providers).
items.fcm: push notifications that tell the Android app there are messages to send.
items.googleCloud: depending on the operator's setup, for example the task queue (Cloud Tasks) or attachment storage (Cloud Storage).
items.smtp: sending notification emails (optional; chosen by the operator).
items.turnstile: bot protection on some features, such as message search (optional).
items.soketi: real-time dashboard updates. It is usually hosted by the operator, so that data stays on their infrastructure.
items.discord: only if you connect the Discord integration (optional).
items.androidApp: depending on how it was built, the Android app may send crash reports (Sentry) and usage statistics (Google Analytics for Firebase).

providers.closing: In addition, your mobile carrier processes the SMS you send and receive, and the operator may use other hosting or database providers. If you need the details, ask the operator of the installation.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.p1: The web dashboard uses very little storage in your browser, and only to work:

session.label: Firebase Authentication session:
session.text: Firebase keeps your session in the browser's storage so you don't have to sign in every time.

preferences.label: Preferences in localStorage:
preferences.text: for example, the last sign-in method you used (httpsms_last_login_method) or whether you prefer to open your conversations directly (httpsms_redirect_to_threads).

turnstile.label: Cloudflare Turnstile:
turnstile.text: if the installation uses it, it may store its own technical data to check that you are not a bot.

cookies.closing: httpSMS does not use advertising cookies. You can clear cookies and local storage from your browser; if you do, you will be signed out and these preferences will be lost.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
retention.p1: Data is kept while your account exists or until you delete it. From the dashboard you can delete messages, threads, phones and webhooks at any time.
retention.p2: You can also delete your account from the {settings} page. When you do, the server deletes your account and its associated data (phones, messages, threads, contacts, heartbeats, API keys, webhooks, integrations and send schedules) and removes your Firebase Authentication user.
retention.p3: Copies may remain for some time in backups, technical logs or third-party services, according to the policies of the installation's operator.

security.title: Security
security.p1: The operator is responsible for securing their installation: keeping the software up to date, using HTTPS, restricting access to the server and database, and making backups.
security.p2: You are responsible for protecting your credentials and API keys. If you think a key has leaked, rotate it from the {settings} page. No system is completely secure, and the software makes no security guarantees.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: Depending on the laws of your country, you may have the right to access, correct or delete your personal data, or to object to its processing (for example, ARCO rights in Mexico or the rights granted by the GDPR in the European Union).
rights.p2: You can exercise many of these rights yourself from the dashboard. For any other request, contact the operator of the installation, who holds your data.

children.title: Minors
children.p1: httpSMS is a technical tool that is not aimed at minors. Operators should not let minors use it without the authorization and supervision required by applicable law.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.p1: This policy may be updated along with the software; the last-updated date is shown at the top of the page. Each operator may adapt their copy, and the version published on their installation is the one that applies to it.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: For questions, bugs or suggestions about the software, open an issue in {issues}. The project has no support email. Issues are public: do not share personal data or API keys in them.
contact.p2: For questions or requests about your data on a specific installation, contact whoever operates it. The project maintainers cannot view, change or delete data on installations they do not run.

terms.metaDescription: Terms of use for httpSMS, free self-hosted software that turns an Android phone into an SMS gateway: responsibilities, prohibited uses and no warranty.
terms.title: Terms and Conditions

intro.p1: These terms govern the use of httpSMS and of the installation where you are reading them. By installing, accessing or using httpSMS, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use it.
intro.p2: We call the person or organization that installs and runs an httpSMS installation the “operator”, anyone with an account on it a “user”, and the people who develop and contribute to the open-source project the “maintainers”.

about.title: What httpSMS is
about.p1: httpSMS is free and open-source software that turns an Android phone into an SMS gateway. It lets you send and receive text messages from your own applications through an HTTP API, webhooks and a web dashboard.
about.p2: It is 100% free and anyone can install it on their own server. There are no paid plans, payments or subscriptions. Messages are sent from your phone's SIM, so sending costs depend on your mobile carrier.

license.title: Open-source license
license.p1: The source code is available on {repo} and is distributed under the {license}. These terms do not limit the rights that license grants you; as far as the software is concerned, the license prevails in case of any conflict.
license.p2: If you modify the software and offer it to other people over a network, the AGPL-3.0 requires you to make the source code of your modified version available to them.

operators.title: Each installation is run by whoever deploys it
operators.p1: There is no central httpSMS service. Each installation is managed by its own operator, who decides who can sign up, how it is configured and which third-party services it uses. The operator is responsible for their installation and may publish additional terms.
operators.p2: The project maintainers only publish the software. They do not run, monitor or control third-party installations, nor the messages sent through them.

responsibilities.title: Operator and user responsibilities
responsibilities.p1: Whoever runs an installation and whoever uses it are solely responsible for:

items.i1: Complying with applicable laws, including telecommunications, personal data protection and marketing or unsolicited messaging laws (for example, in Mexico the Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties and PROFECO's REPEP do-not-contact registry; in the United States the TCPA; in the European Union the GDPR).
items.i2: Obtaining the consent of the people they message when the law requires it, and honoring their requests to stop receiving messages.
items.i3: Following their mobile carrier's terms, including its sending limits and its rules on bulk or commercial messages.
items.i4: The content of every message sent from their accounts and phones.
items.i5: SIM and phone plan costs, and the consequences of misuse, such as the line being blocked or suspended.
items.i6: Server security: keeping the software up to date, using HTTPS, protecting the database and making backups.
items.i7: Keeping API keys and credentials secret, and rotating them if they leak. Anything done with a key is considered done by its owner.
items.i8: Keeping the Android phone on, charged, connected to the internet and with the permissions the app needs.

prohibited.title: Prohibited uses
prohibited.p1: You may not use httpSMS to:

items.i1: Send spam or unsolicited bulk messages, including advertising without consent.
items.i2: Commit fraud, phishing or smishing, impersonate other people or organizations, or deceive recipients.
items.i3: Harass, threaten, extort or intimidate anyone.
items.i4: Send illegal content, including content that infringes the rights of others or exploits minors.
items.i6: Bypass carrier limits, filters or controls, for example through SIM farms or unauthorized traffic routes.
items.i7: Collect or process personal data unlawfully.

suspension.title: Account suspension and termination
